page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The statement
lines: Raoult's law states that, at a given
temperature, the partial vapour pressure of
each volatile component of a solution is
directly proportional to its mole fraction
p₁⁰ = vapour pressure of the pure liquid 1
steps.why: The law fixes how much of each liquid goes into the vapour. Only the fraction of the surface made up of one component can send that component into the vapour, so its vapour pressure is its pure value multiplied by its mole fraction. Every result later in this chapter — lowering of vapour pressure, elevation of boiling point, depression of freezing point — is built on this one line.
common_mistakes: Writing that the vapour pressure is proportional to the mass of the component. It is proportional to the mole fraction, not to the mass.
Leaving out the words "at a given temperature". Vapour pressure changes with temperature, so the condition is part of the statement.
steps.memory_tip: Each liquid gives its own pure vapour pressure, scaled down by its mole fraction.
steps.margin_note: The words "directly proportional" plus "mole fraction" are what earn this mark. A statement with no mole fraction in it earns nothing.

steps.label: Non-volatile solute form
lines: When the solute is non-volatile, only the
solvent goes into the vapour. The law then
takes the form used in this chapter:
p⁰ = vapour pressure of the pure solvent
pₛ = vapour pressure of the solution
x₂ = mole fraction of the solute
steps.why: A non-volatile solute has no vapour pressure of its own, so the vapour pressure of the solution is only the solvent's share, pₛ = p⁰x₁. Since x₁ + x₂ = 1, subtracting gives (p⁰ − pₛ)/p⁰ = x₂. The left side is called the relative lowering of vapour pressure, and it is the quantity used to find molar masses.
common_mistakes: Writing x₁, the mole fraction of the solvent, on the right side. The relative lowering equals the mole fraction of the SOLUTE.
Dropping the p⁰ in the denominator. Without it the quantity is the lowering, not the RELATIVE lowering.
steps.memory_tip: Relative lowering on the left, mole fraction of the solute on the right.
steps.margin_note: Box the equation and define all three symbols under it. The symbol list carries half of this mark.

insider_note: Most answers stop at the sentence and never write the equation. A full answer to this question is a sentence and a formula, so write both even though the question only says "state".
